R0019.title: Unauthorized Account Sharing
R0019.definition: Illegally selling or sharing paid account privileges that support multi-device login to others.
R0019.description: Malicious actors exploit the ability to log into accounts on multiple devices simultaneously, selling accounts with paid privileges to multiple people at low prices to profit from the price difference. The platform's multi-device login feature is intended for a single user with multiple devices, not for different users sharing the same privileges. Instead of earning multiple paid subscriptions, the platform earns only one while black market operators profit from the price arbitrage.
R0019.influence: Causes economic losses to the platform.

references.title: Breaking the Account Theft-Breeding-Sale Black Market: Strengthening Legal and Technical Defenses

observables: The number of simultaneous online devices for a single membership account exceeds a reasonable personal-use threshold
Account login IP geolocation jumps across regions within a short window, inconsistent with a single person's movement patterns
The account is used or played concurrently across multiple devices, with behavior matching shared-resale platform signatures
Login device fingerprints for the shared account change frequently and are linked to a large number of unfamiliar devices
The membership account is linked to transactions or customer-service contacts from third-party sharing-resale pages
